senses.definition: To keep reminding or asking someone about something in a way that can be annoying.
senses.example: I promised to pack my lunch so my brother would stop nagging me about it.

senses.definition: A small pointed piece of metal used to hold things together.
senses.example: A nail held the two boards in place.

senses.definition: The hard covering at the tip of a finger or toe.
senses.example: I got blue paint on one nail.

senses.definition: To fasten something with nails.
senses.example: We helped Dad nail the loose board back in place.

senses.definition: A person or thing that shares another's name, often because one was named after the other.
senses.example: The boat had a surprising namesake, my aunt's cat.

senses.definition: A card or label someone wears to show their name.
senses.example: I wore a bright nametag at the first meeting of our club.

senses.definition: A small piece of cloth or paper used to wipe hands or lips during a meal.
senses.example: I wiped the jam off my fingers with a napkin.

senses.definition: The voice or person that tells a story.
senses.example: In this book, the narrator is the family’s dog.

senses.definition: Not far from one side to the other.
senses.example: Only one person could walk through the narrow gate at a time.

senses.definition: To make something smaller in width, range, or number.
senses.example: We narrowed our choices to three games.

senses.definition: Very unpleasant to sense or experience.
senses.example: There was a nasty smell coming from the spoiled fruit.

senses.definition: Mean or rude.
senses.example: A nasty comment made the new player feel unwelcome.

senses.definition: Living or growing naturally in a place without being brought there from somewhere else.
senses.example: We planted native flowers for local bees.

senses.definition: Connected with the place where someone was born or grew up.
senses.example: My aunt went back to visit her native town.

senses.definition: A plant that occurs naturally in a particular area without having been brought there by people.
senses.example: We chose a native plant that local butterflies can use.

senses.definition: A legal process through which someone becomes a citizen of a country after birth.
senses.example: At the end of naturalization, the new citizens took an oath.

senses.definition: The living things and physical features of Earth, such as forests, rivers, and rocks.
senses.example: We kept a notebook about the nature we saw on the island.

senses.definition: What someone or something is usually like.
senses.example: It is in the dog’s nature to chase anything that rolls.

senses.definition: The part of a country’s armed forces that works mainly at sea.
senses.example: The museum had a ship that once belonged to the navy.

senses.definition: Very dark blue.
senses.example: I wore a navy shirt for the concert.

senses.definition: Close to a thing, place, point, or time.
senses.example: We live near the school.

senses.definition: Close in distance or time.
senses.example: The nearest bench was across the path.

senses.definition: To get closer to something.
senses.example: The players cheered as they neared the finish.

senses.definition: Close to this or that place.
senses.example: We heard the ducks splashing somewhere nearby.

senses.definition: Not far away from a particular place.
senses.example: A nearby tree gave our group some shade.

senses.definition: Tidy or arranged in an orderly way.
senses.example: We stacked our clean shirts in neat piles.

senses.definition: Pleasing, interesting, or fun.
senses.example: The new museum had a neat model of a working lock.

senses.definition: An enormous cloud of gas, dust or both in space.
senses.example: Young stars were forming inside the cloudy nebula.

senses.definition: Needed for something to happen or work.
senses.example: Warm clothes are necessary for a long walk in the snow.

senses.definition: A chain, band, or string of things worn around the neck for decoration.
senses.example: She made a necklace from shells she found at the beach.

senses.definition: A decorative strip of cloth tied around the neck, often worn with a shirt collar.
senses.example: My uncle wore a blue necktie for the concert.

senses.definition: A sweet liquid made by many flowers that some animals drink for food.
senses.example: The hummingbird used its tongue to drink nectar.

senses.definition: A narrow part of a flower that can hold sweet nectar at its tip or along its inside.
senses.example: A hummingbird can reach into a columbine's nectar spur.

senses.definition: To have to have or do something.
senses.example: We need a larger bag for all the blocks.

senses.definition: Something that is wanted so strongly or matters so much that it is required.
senses.example: The shelter helps meet people’s basic needs, including food and a place to sleep.

senses.definition: A group of needle-shaped leaves that grow together from a single point.
senses.example: An eastern white pine usually grows five needles in each needle bundle.

senses.definition: A number less than zero.
senses.example: A temperature of minus five degrees is written with a negative number.

senses.definition: To fail to do something important or give someone or something the care it needs.
senses.example: I neglected to charge my camera, so it stopped working before the show.

senses.definition: A person who lives near you.
senses.example: Our neighbor waved as we walked past her yard.

senses.definition: A place or thing next to another of its kind.
senses.example: Canada is a neighbor of the United States.

senses.definition: Not one and not the other of two people or things.
senses.example: Neither door was open.

senses.definition: Used with “nor” to show that both choices are ruled out.
senses.example: We saw neither the cat nor the dog outside.

senses.definition: A son of your brother or sister, or of the brother or sister of your spouse.
senses.example: My aunt took her nephew to the science museum.

senses.definition: A tiny part of a kidney that filters the blood, then takes useful material back.
senses.example: Some water passes into a tube inside a nephron.

senses.definition: Worried, unsure, or uneasy about what may happen.
senses.example: I was nervous before reading my poem aloud.

senses.definition: Related to the nerves that carry messages in the body.
senses.example: The brain and nerves are parts of the nervous system.

senses.definition: A place an animal makes or uses for laying eggs, raising young, or resting.
senses.example: A robin built a nest in the fork of the tree.

senses.definition: To build, use, or settle in a nest.
senses.example: Two birds nested on a ledge near our window.

senses.definition: To fit one thing inside another of the same shape.
senses.example: The bowls nest together, so they take up less room.

senses.definition: A box built to give an animal a sheltered place to raise its young.
senses.example: A female wood duck used the nest box set near the pond.

senses.definition: The hollow, rounded part of a nest where the eggs or young can sit.
senses.example: A barn swallow uses mud to shape its nest cup.

senses.definition: To settle into a comfortable or sheltered place.
senses.example: The kitten nestled into the blankets.

senses.definition: A material made from cords joined to leave many holes, or an object made of it.
senses.example: The ball bounced into the basketball net.

senses.definition: To catch something in a net.
senses.example: The park worker netted a leaf that was floating in the pool.

senses.definition: A collection of devices linked so they can share information.
senses.example: Our classroom computers can connect to a network and share a printer.

senses.definition: A nerve cell that carries a message in the body.
senses.example: A neuron can send a signal to another neuron.

senses.definition: A very dense object left when the center of some massive stars collapses.
senses.example: A spinning neutron star can send a beam that appears to flash from Earth.

senses.definition: Not at any time.
senses.example: I have never seen snow in July.

senses.definition: Even though something just said might make you expect a different result.
senses.example: It was windy. Nevertheless, we decided to stay outside.

senses.definition: Made, started, or found recently.
senses.example: A new library opened near our school.

senses.definition: Different from what you had or knew before.
senses.example: We learned a new way to fold the paper boat.

senses.definition: Someone who has recently arrived or started in a place or group.
senses.example: As a newcomer to the club, I asked where to put my coat.

senses.definition: Information about something that has happened recently.
senses.example: The school shared news about the book fair on its website.

senses.definition: A printed or online publication that reports the news and may include opinions, games, or ads.
senses.example: Grandpa sent me a newspaper story about the library.

senses.definition: A type of salamander that spends some or all of its life in water.
senses.example: A newt swam past the reeds.

senses.definition: Coming right after this one or nearest to it.
senses.example: The next bus will get here in five minutes.

senses.definition: At the time immediately after now or after something else.
senses.example: What should we try next?

senses.definition: Almost nothing, especially when talking about an amount or cost.
senses.example: The used picture frame cost next to nothing at the school sale.

senses.definition: To eat using small bites.
senses.example: The rabbit nibbled a piece of lettuce.

senses.definition: A small bite of food.
senses.example: I took a nibble of the muffin while it was still warm.

senses.definition: Pleasant or enjoyable.
senses.example: It was nice to sit in the sun after lunch.

senses.definition: Kind or polite.
senses.example: It was nice of you to remember her name.

senses.definition: A name people use in place of a person’s or thing’s regular name, often for fun or affection.
senses.example: My cousin’s nickname is Cricket because she is always jumping.

senses.definition: To give or call someone or something by an extra name.
senses.example: The team nicknamed their new mascot Bubbles.

senses.definition: A daughter of your brother or sister, or of the brother or sister of your spouse.
senses.example: My uncle took his niece to her first baseball game.

senses.definition: The part of each day between evening and morning when the Sun is below the horizon.
senses.example: At night we could see stars above the trees.

senses.definition: The time in the evening when daylight fades and night starts.
senses.example: We reached the campsite just before nightfall.

senses.definition: A frightening or very upsetting dream.
senses.example: My nightmare about a giant spider woke me up.

senses.definition: Able to move quickly and easily, or quick to think and act.
senses.example: The nimble squirrel hopped from one branch to another.

senses.definition: A gas that makes up most of Earth’s air and is found in many living things.
senses.example: The air we breathe contains nitrogen as well as oxygen.

senses.definition: No person at all.
senses.example: Nobody was on the court when we arrived.

senses.definition: A sound, especially one that is loud, unpleasant, or hard to understand.
senses.example: A tapping noise drew my attention to the window.

senses.definition: Reducing a sound by making waves that partly cancel its pressure changes.
senses.example: The headphones used noise cancellation to make the motor hum harder to hear.

senses.definition: Making or full of loud sounds.
senses.example: The cafeteria got noisy as more students came in.

senses.definition: Not any of the people or things being talked about.
senses.example: I checked all four hooks, but none held my jacket.

senses.definition: Words or ideas that have no clear meaning or are not reasonable.
senses.example: The message about penguins flying to the Moon was nonsense.

senses.definition: Going on without a break.
senses.example: Our bus made a nonstop trip to the museum.

senses.definition: Without taking a break.
senses.example: The younger kids talked nonstop until we reached the playground.

senses.definition: A small corner or sheltered spot.
senses.example: My favorite reading nook is behind the living room chair.

senses.definition: Twelve o’clock in the middle of the day.
senses.example: The food truck opens at noon.

senses.definition: Usual or expected in the situation.
senses.example: School will open at its normal time tomorrow.

senses.definition: A usual or expected state or amount.
senses.example: The water level returned to normal after the storm.

senses.definition: The direction opposite south, roughly toward Earth’s North Pole.
senses.example: We used a compass to find north.

senses.definition: Toward or in the north.
senses.example: We drove north until we reached the bridge.

senses.definition: The part of the face used for breathing and smelling.
senses.example: A drop of rain landed on the tip of my nose.

senses.definition: The front end of an aircraft or another long object.
senses.example: The pilot pointed the nose of the plane toward the runway.

senses.definition: A way to write down information with a set of signs or symbols.
senses.example: Musical notation shows which notes to play and how long to play them.

senses.definition: A short piece of writing used as a message or reminder.
senses.example: I left a note on the table saying where I had gone.

senses.definition: A musical sound of a particular pitch, or the sign used to write it.
senses.example: The first note of our song was easy to sing.

senses.definition: To notice, write down, or point out something.
senses.example: Please note which plants have begun to flower.

senses.definition: A book of blank or lined pages for writing and drawing.
senses.example: I kept the bird list in my notebook.

senses.definition: To see, hear, or become aware of something.
senses.example: Did you notice the tiny tracks in the snow?

senses.definition: A message that gives information, often put where people can see it.
senses.example: A notice at the library said it would close early.

senses.definition: An idea, thought, or belief about something.
senses.example: My notion that owls only lived in forests changed when I spotted one near town.

senses.definition: A word that can name someone or something, such as a person, place, object, or idea.
senses.example: The word “river” is a noun because it names a kind of waterway.

senses.definition: A long made-up story in a book or digital form.
senses.example: The novel tells a story about two friends who find an old boat.

senses.definition: New and different from what people are used to.
senses.example: We tried a novel way to build a tower using folded paper.

senses.definition: A person who is just beginning to learn or do something.
senses.example: As a novice at chess, I still needed help setting up the pieces.

senses.definition: A short piece at the end of a tube that directs a flow of liquid, air, or gas.
senses.example: I turned the nozzle to make a gentler spray of water.

senses.definition: A central part of many cells that holds most of their DNA.
senses.example: Chromosomes fit inside the nucleus.

senses.definition: To push someone or something gently.
senses.example: Our dog nudged the ball toward me with her nose.

senses.definition: To encourage someone gently to do something.
senses.example: Rae nudged me to ask the librarian for help.

senses.definition: A small gentle push or reminder.
senses.example: A nudge from my elbow told Jo that the show was about to start.

senses.definition: A small lump of material or food, such as a piece of gold or a small piece of chicken.
senses.example: A tiny gold nugget glittered in the miner's pan.

senses.definition: Someone or something that causes annoyance or small problems.
senses.example: The loose wheel was a nuisance because it rattled all the way home.

senses.definition: Unable to feel touch, heat, cold, or pain normally in a body part.
senses.example: My toes felt numb after a long time in the snow.

senses.definition: To make a body part lose some or all feeling for a time.
senses.example: The cold water numbed my fingers.

senses.definition: A value used to count, measure, or put things in order.
senses.example: The number six tells how many crates we need.

senses.definition: A group of digits that names or identifies something.
senses.example: The bus number was printed above the door.

senses.definition: To give each item in a group a number.
senses.example: Please number the pages before you hand them in.

senses.definition: A line with marked spots showing where numbers are in order and how far apart they are.
senses.example: On a number line, 1/2 is halfway between 0 and 1.

senses.definition: The top number in a fraction, showing how many of the equal-size parts are counted.
senses.example: In 3/4, the numerator is 3.

senses.definition: Very many or existing in large numbers.
senses.example: Numerous small shells washed onto the beach.

senses.definition: A fallen tree that gives new plants a place to grow as its wood breaks down.
senses.example: Three young trees grew in a row on the old nurse log.

senses.definition: A room or place where young children are cared for.
senses.example: We picked up the baby from the nursery after the meeting.

senses.definition: A place where young plants are grown and often sold.
senses.example: The nursery sold small trees in pots.

senses.definition: A dry seed or fruit with a hard covering, such as a walnut or acorn.
senses.example: A squirrel hurried away with a nut.

senses.definition: A small metal part with a hole that screws onto a bolt to hold things in place.
senses.example: The missing nut fell off the wheel.

senses.definition: A substance that a living thing needs to grow, get energy, or stay healthy.
senses.example: Calcium is a nutrient that helps build strong bones.

senses.definition: Information on packaged food about the amount of energy and certain nutrients it contains.
senses.example: I read the nutrition label to find out how much fiber is listed.

senses.definition: To press or rub the nose or face gently against something.
senses.example: The puppy nuzzled my hand before it fell asleep.
